When `py_version` is requested on a supported runtime and `uv` is not preinstalled globally, Conan should still be able to create the requested versioned environment without requiring a separate manual `uv` setup step.

task_19.title: Add built-in xz and zstd compression support for Conan artifacts
task_19.description: Conan 2.25.0 adds experimental built-in support for `xz` and `zstd` artifact compression in addition to gzip. Users can choose the upload compression format and cache archive extension, and Conan can download and unpack supported compressed recipe and package artifacts while rejecting incompatible or corrupted remote contents.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan supports built-in `gz`, `xz`, and `zst` compression for uploaded and cache-saved artifacts, and that consumers receive clear compatibility failures or warnings when a selected format is experimental, unsupported by their Python runtime, or stored ambiguously on a remote.

expectation.grounded: Conan must accept `core.upload:compression_format` with `gz` (default), `xz`, or `zst` for recipe export, export-sources, and package archives. `core:compresslevel` should apply as the generic compression-level setting, with `core.gzip:compresslevel` still honored for gzip when the generic setting is unset. `conan cache save` must infer the compression format from the output archive extension (`.tgz`, `.txz`, `.tzst`) and create a matching archive; `conan cache restore` must accept archives in those formats. Upload, download, and install flows must recognize the corresponding `conan_export`, `conan_sources`, and `conan_package` compressed artifact filenames, automatically unpack supported formats, warn that `xz` and `zst` are experimental, reject `zst` creation or consumption on Python versions below 3.14, and fail when a remote contains multiple compressed variants for the same artifact.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose a built-in compression format for Conan artifacts and cache archives without external tooling, continue consuming those artifacts transparently when their environment supports the format, and receive explicit warnings or errors when the chosen format is experimental, incompatible, or the remote artifact set is inconsistent.

constraints.grounded: Default behavior must remain gzip-based when no new format is selected. Consumers of older Conan versions may be unable to install `xz` or `zst` artifacts, and `zst` must be unavailable on Python versions below 3.14. Remote recipe or package snapshots with duplicate compressed files for a single artifact must be treated as corrupted instead of selecting one arbitrarily. Existing prepared compressed artifacts in the local cache should not be silently replaced by a different format during upload preparation.
constraints.conceptual: The new compression support must preserve backward-compatible defaults, avoid guessing between conflicting artifact variants, and prevent users from producing or consuming formats their runtime cannot safely handle.

behavior: Conan can create uploaded recipe, export-sources, and package archives using `gz`, `xz`, or `zst` compression instead of gzip-only artifacts.
The configured upload format determines the compressed artifact filename suffixes that Conan produces and uploads for exports, sources, and packages.
Conan emits experimental warnings when `xz` or `zst` compression is selected.
`zst` artifact creation and decompression are blocked on Python runtimes below 3.14 with a Conan error instead of attempting a broken operation.
`conan cache save` supports `.tgz`, `.txz`, and `.tzst` output archives and uses the archive extension to choose compression.
Conan download and install flows locate and unpack the single available compressed recipe, sources, or package artifact regardless of whether it is gzip, xz, or zstd.
If a remote contains more than one compressed variant for the same recipe export, recipe sources, or package artifact, Conan treats the remote contents as corrupted and aborts.
If a compatible compressed artifact already exists in the local prepared upload area, Conan reuses that artifact instead of regenerating it in another format.
acceptance_criteria: When a user uploads packages with `core.upload:compression_format=xz`, Conan should produce and upload `.txz` recipe and package artifacts and warn that the format is experimental.
When a user uploads packages with `core.upload:compression_format=zst` on Python 3.14 or newer, Conan should produce and upload `.tzst` artifacts and warn that the format is experimental.
When a user selects `core.upload:compression_format=zst` on Python lower than 3.14, Conan should stop with a Conan error before creating or uploading `zst` artifacts.

When a user installs or downloads artifacts that were uploaded as `.tgz`, `.txz`, or `.tzst`, Conan should fetch the matching compressed artifact and unpack it into the normal recipe or package contents when the runtime supports that format.
When a user restores a cache archive saved as `.tgz`, `.txz`, or `.tzst`, Conan should accept the archive and restore the contained cache contents.
When a remote exposes two compressed variants for the same exported recipe, sources bundle, or package bundle, Conan should fail the operation and report the remote artifact set as corrupted.
When no compression format is configured, Conan should continue using gzip artifacts by default.

task_20.title: Fail fast for unsupported PyEnv version selection
task_20.description: Conan 2.25.0 updates Python environment management so version-pinned PyEnv creation validates the host interpreter before attempting UV-based environment setup. This prevents late failures when a recipe requests a specific Python version from a Conan process that is itself running on an unsupported Python release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that requesting a specific Python version through PyEnv only proceeds when the running Conan interpreter supports that workflow. Ensure that unsupported host Python versions fail immediately and clearly instead of failing later during virtual-environment creation.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.system.PyEnv` is constructed with the `py_version` argument, it should validate that Conan is running on Python 3.8 or newer before attempting the UV-backed virtual-environment path. If the host interpreter is older than Python 3.8, initialization should raise `ConanException` immediately. Using `PyEnv` without `py_version` should continue to use the normal virtual-environment creation flow with the configured or discovered Python interpreter.
expectation.conceptual: Users can request a specific Python version for an isolated Conan-managed environment only when the current Conan runtime supports that capability. If the current runtime is too old, the operation should stop at setup time with a clear error, while ordinary environment creation without version selection should keep working as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the behavior of `PyEnv` callers that omit `py_version`. Preserve existing interpreter discovery and configured interpreter usage, and keep version-selected environment creation on supported runtimes using the existing public error mechanism (`ConanException`) when setup cannot proceed.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to compatibility validation for version-selected Python environments. Existing non-versioned environment workflows and supported version-selection flows should remain behaviorally consistent.

behavior: Constructing `PyEnv` with `py_version` on a Conan runtime older than Python 3.8 fails immediately with `ConanException` before any virtual-environment bootstrap is attempted.
Constructing `PyEnv` without `py_version` continues through the standard virtual-environment path and is not blocked by the UV compatibility check.
On supported Conan runtimes, `PyEnv(py_version=...)` continues to create a version-specific environment through the version-selection workflow rather than falling back to an unversioned environment.
The user-visible failure point for unsupported version selection moves to initialization time, making the incompatibility explicit before package installation or build commands run.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe initializes `PyEnv(..., py_version="<requested version>")` while Conan is running under Python 3.7 or earlier, it should stop immediately with `ConanException` indicating that version-selected PyEnv requires Python 3.8 or newer.
When a recipe initializes `PyEnv(...)` without specifying `py_version` on the same older Conan runtime, it should still create and use a regular virtual environment.

When Conan is running under Python 3.8 or newer and a recipe initializes `PyEnv(..., py_version="<requested version>")`, the requested version-selection workflow should proceed and make that environment available to subsequent Conan recipe steps.
When version-selected environment creation is unsupported, the failure should happen before any downstream package installation or recipe build command depends on the environment.

task_22.title: Default to dnf on AlmaLinux, Rocky, and Oracle Linux
task_22.description: The library updates its default Linux system package manager detection so AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and Oracle Linux use dnf instead of the legacy yum mapping. This aligns package installation behavior with current platform defaults when consumers rely on automatic package manager selection.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that automatic system package manager selection uses `dnf` by default on AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and Oracle Linux instead of `yum`.

expectation.grounded: When Conan resolves the default system package manager from the detected operating system or Linux distribution, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and Oracle Linux must map to `dnf` rather than `yum`. Existing package manager defaults for other mapped distributions should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users on AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, and Oracle Linux should see Conan choose the modern default package manager automatically. Package installation flows that depend on automatic manager detection should invoke `dnf` on those platforms instead of falling back to the older `yum` behavior.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to the default distro-to-manager mapping for automatic selection. It must not alter unrelated mappings such as `apt-get`, `apk`, `brew`, `pacman`, `choco`, or existing `yum` assignments for other distributions like Amazon Linux, Pidora, Scientific Linux, or XenServer.
constraints.conceptual: Only the affected Linux distributions should change behavior. Other operating systems and Linux distributions should continue using their current default package manager selection without regression.

behavior: Automatic package manager detection now resolves AlmaLinux to `dnf`.
Automatic package manager detection now resolves Rocky Linux to `dnf`.
Automatic package manager detection now resolves Oracle Linux to `dnf`.
These distributions are no longer treated as `yum`-based by default during system package manager selection.
Previously supported default mappings for other distributions remain as before.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan runs on AlmaLinux and a system package manager tool relies on automatic manager detection, it should select `dnf` as the default manager.
When Conan runs on Rocky Linux and a system package manager tool relies on automatic manager detection, it should select `dnf` as the default manager.
When Conan runs on Oracle Linux and a system package manager tool relies on automatic manager detection, it should select `dnf` as the default manager.
When Conan performs automatic manager detection on distributions that still map to `yum`, it should continue selecting `yum`.

When Conan performs automatic manager detection on distributions mapped to other managers such as `apt-get`, `apk`, `pacman`, `brew`, or `choco`, their selected default manager should remain unchanged.

task_21.title: Restore legacy CMake definition variables in CMakeConfigDeps
task_21.description: Conan 2.25.0 updates CMakeConfigDeps so generated package config files expose legacy `<library>_DEFINITIONS` variables from declared Conan preprocessor defines. This restores compatibility with older CMake consumers and symbol-detection flows that still rely on those variables instead of only imported target properties.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.25.0 preserves compatibility for CMake consumers that rely on legacy `<library>_DEFINITIONS` variables, so packages declaring preprocessor defines continue to work with older symbol checks and similar CMake logic.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps generates config files for a dependency that declares `cpp_info.defines`, it should populate the legacy `<library>_DEFINITIONS` variable from the aggregated defines exposed by that package. Older CMake flows such as `check_symbol_exists()` and similar compile-time probes should be able to observe those definitions through the generated config, in addition to the existing imported target metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake package files should continue to support both modern target-based consumers and older CMake code that reads package definition variables directly. Any preprocessor definitions declared by the package should be visible to legacy symbol-detection and compatibility logic after the upgrade.

constraints.grounded: This is a backward-compatibility fix in CMakeConfigDeps output. It should not remove or replace existing imported targets, include directory exposure, or library linkage information. Packages without declared defines should remain consumable, and packages with declared defines should expose the full aggregated set through the legacy variable interface.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add missing compatibility data without changing the normal dependency consumption model. Existing consumers should keep working, and legacy consumers should gain the missing definition visibility rather than needing a different integration pattern.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps-generated package config files now export legacy `<library>_DEFINITIONS` values based on the dependency's declared Conan preprocessor definitions.
The exported legacy definitions reflect the aggregated definition set for the generated package configuration rather than being left empty.
Older CMake checks that depend on package definition variables, including symbol-detection style probes, can observe those definitions after loading the generated config.
Modern imported target usage remains available; this change supplements compatibility behavior rather than replacing target-based metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency declares one or more Conan `cpp_info.defines` values and a consumer installs `CMakeConfigDeps`, the generated package config should expose those values through the corresponding legacy `<library>_DEFINITIONS` variable.

When consumer CMake code performs an older symbol or compile-feature probe that depends on the package's preprocessor definitions, it should receive the same definition visibility after loading the generated config.
When a consumer uses the generated imported targets as before, include paths and link information should continue to behave consistently with prior releases.
When a dependency does not declare preprocessor defines, generating and consuming its CMakeConfigDeps output should continue to work without requiring legacy definition data.

task_23.title: Preserve package names in no-op system package install output
task_23.description: Conan 2.25.0 fixes the system package manager install flow so that when an install request becomes a no-op because the required packages are already considered installed, the user-facing output still shows which packages were requested instead of losing that package list.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that system package manager installs still report the requested package names when Conan skips the install as already satisfied, so users can see which system requirements were evaluated even when no package manager action is taken.

expectation.grounded: When Conan system package manager helpers handle an install request that does not execute a package manager install because the requested packages are already recorded as installed, the informational 'already installed' output should include the original requested package names. This behavior should apply to the no-op branch of the install flow in `conan.tools.system.package_manager` without changing the install command path or exception behavior.
expectation.conceptual: If Conan determines that a system requirement install does not need to run, it should still clearly tell the user which packages were considered already satisfied rather than emitting an empty or unclear result.

constraints.grounded: Do not change when Conan decides to skip installation, how it invokes the package manager, which exit codes are accepted, or how failed substitute installs raise errors. The change is limited to preserving the originally requested package names for the no-op informational output.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the existing install and error behavior intact. Only improve the accuracy of the user-visible status reported for skipped system package installs.

behavior: The system package manager install flow retains the original package names requested by the caller for later reporting.
If the install operation becomes a no-op because there are no packages left to install, Conan emits an informational already-installed status that names the originally requested packages.
The behavior of actual install execution remains unchanged when packages still need to be installed.
Error handling for unsuccessful package substitute installation attempts remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan system package manager helper is asked to install one or more packages that are already considered installed, it should report those package names in the already-installed output even though no install command runs.
When the no-op path is taken for multiple requested packages, the output should identify the full set of requested package names rather than an empty list.
When packages still need installation, Conan should continue to run the package manager install flow as before.
When all substitute installation attempts fail, Conan should continue to raise the existing installation failure exception.

task_24.title: Align workspace lockfile generation with supported commands
task_24.description: The workspace CLI now distinguishes between commands that only consume an existing lockfile and the command that can actually produce an updated lockfile. Orchestrated workspace install, build, complete, and create flows should no longer expose lockfile output generation options, while workspace super-install should update and save the resulting lockfile when those options are requested.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspace commands only expose lockfile behaviors they can actually perform. Orchestrated workspace install/build/complete/create flows must accept an existing lockfile for dependency resolution but must not offer lockfile generation output options, and workspace super-install must be the command that writes any updated lockfile state.

expectation.grounded: The `conan workspace install`, `conan workspace build`, `conan workspace complete`, and `conan workspace create` commands should accept `--lockfile` and `--lockfile-partial` as input-only lockfile options. These commands should no longer accept lockfile generation arguments such as `--lockfile-out`, and they should not attempt to update or save a lockfile as part of the orchestrated workflow. When these commands invoke underlying `install` or `build` operations, they should continue propagating the selected input lockfile context so dependency resolution stays consistent. The `conan workspace super-install` command should update the computed lockfile with the resolved graph and save it when lockfile output options are provided.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace commands that only orchestrate installs and builds should behave as consumers of an existing lockfile, not producers of a new one. Users should only be able to generate or refresh a workspace lockfile through the dedicated workspace command that resolves the full graph and persists the result.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress support for reading a workspace lockfile via `--lockfile`, including explicit empty lockfile selection behavior, and keep `--lockfile-partial` available for partial lockfile resolution in the affected workspace commands. Do not present output-generation flags on commands that cannot persist a lockfile. Preserve lockfile update and save behavior for `workspace super-install`, including support for lockfile package filtering and clean/update semantics when that command is used.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing lockfile consumption behavior intact while removing misleading output-generation options from commands that cannot produce a lockfile. Lockfile creation or refresh must remain available only where the CLI can actually save a resolved result.

behavior: `conan workspace install`, `conan workspace build`, `conan workspace complete`, and `conan workspace create` treat lockfiles as input-only state.
Those orchestrated workspace commands continue to support reading an existing lockfile and optional partial resolution, but they no longer expose lockfile output-generation arguments.
Supplying a lockfile output-generation flag to an orchestrated workspace command is rejected at the CLI argument level instead of being silently accepted.
When an orchestrated workspace command dispatches nested install or build operations, it forwards the chosen input lockfile context so those operations resolve against the same lockfile state.
`conan workspace super-install` updates the lockfile from the resolved dependency graph and persists it when the user requests lockfile output.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan workspace install` with `--lockfile` or `--lockfile-partial`, the command should use that lockfile context for resolution without advertising or performing lockfile output generation.
When a user runs `conan workspace build` with an input lockfile, the nested build/install actions should resolve using the same lockfile context.
When a user runs `conan workspace complete` or `conan workspace create` with an input lockfile, the command should consume the lockfile for dependency resolution but should not write a new one.

When a user passes `--lockfile-out` to `conan workspace install`, `conan workspace build`, `conan workspace complete`, or `conan workspace create`, the CLI should reject that argument as unsupported for that command.
When a user runs `conan workspace super-install` with lockfile output options, it should emit an updated lockfile representing the resolved workspace graph.

task_25.title: Reduce Conan sqlite cache lock contention
task_25.description: Conan 2.25.0 narrows the lifetime of sqlite cache database connections so read operations fetch rows before returning results, reducing lock contention and avoiding operational issues caused by connection-scoped iteration. It also converts database lock acquisition timeout failures into a regular ConanException instead of an assertion-style failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan cache reads against the sqlite metadata database do not keep database connections open while callers consume recipe and package results, so concurrent operations are less likely to hit locking or operational failures. Ensure that lock acquisition timeouts are reported as a ConanException rather than as an assertion failure.

expectation.grounded: BaseDbTable.db_connection() should only keep the sqlite connection open for the database execute and fetch stage, with RecipesDBTable and PackagesDBTable methods returning fully materialized results after the connection scope exits. Methods that enumerate recipe or package references or revisions should no longer expose connection-scoped yielded results. Existing lookup contracts should remain intact: get_recipe() and get_latest_recipe() still raise ConanReferenceDoesNotExistInDB for missing recipes, existence checks still return bool, and path/build-id/package lookups still return the same object shape or None when no match exists. If the database lock cannot be acquired within 20 seconds, db_connection() should raise ConanException.
expectation.conceptual: Cache metadata reads should release sqlite resources as soon as the rows have been fetched, instead of keeping the database tied up while results are iterated or converted. Users should see the same successful lookup results and missing-item behavior as before, but with fewer lock-related operational issues and with a normal Conan error when lock contention exceeds the timeout.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the data returned for successful recipe and package lookups. Preserve the existing missing-item semantics: missing recipes still raise ConanReferenceDoesNotExistInDB, missing package/path/build-id matches still return None, and package revision existence checks still return True or False. Keep the lock wait budget at 20 seconds while changing only the failure signaling from assertion-based failure to ConanException.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve robustness under sqlite contention without changing what valid cache queries return or how missing records are represented. Only the connection lifetime and timeout error reporting should change from a user-visible behavior standpoint.

behavior: Recipe and package query operations that previously yielded rows now return fully materialized collections after fetching all rows within the sqlite connection scope.
Single-row cache lookup operations fetch the row while the sqlite connection is open, then perform object construction and return handling after the connection has been released.
Missing recipe lookups continue to raise ConanReferenceDoesNotExistInDB, while absent package, path, and build-id matches continue to return None or False according to the existing API contract.
If the sqlite cache lock cannot be acquired within 20 seconds, Conan raises ConanException instead of failing through an assertion.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan retrieves recipe or package references or revisions from the cache, it should return the complete result set without requiring the caller to keep a sqlite database connection open during result consumption.
When Conan performs cache reads that post-process fetched rows into recipe or package objects, it should do that work after the sqlite connection has already been released.

When a requested recipe is not present in the cache, Conan should still raise ConanReferenceDoesNotExistInDB; when a package, path, or build-id lookup has no match, it should still report no result through None or False as appropriate.
When sqlite cache lock contention prevents acquiring the database lock for 20 seconds, Conan should fail with ConanException rather than an assertion-style error.

task_26.title: Fix cpp_info deduction for mixed component types
task_26.description: The update fixes a runtime failure in cpp_info deduction for multi-component packages. Components that leave their type unset no longer fail when Conan deduces library metadata in the presence of other components that use PackageType values, while explicit invalid component types are still rejected.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that C/C++ package metadata deduction works for multi-component packages when some components define a type and others leave the type unspecified, without failing during dependency generation or explicit cpp_info deduction.

expectation.grounded: When `deduce_full_cpp_info()` evaluates a component that declares libraries, an unset component `.type` must be treated as valid input and must not trigger a `None` versus `PackageType` comparison failure. Automatic deduction must continue for components whose `.type` is `None`, `PackageType.SHARED`, or `PackageType.STATIC`. If a component with libraries explicitly declares a different incompatible type, Conan must still raise `ConanException` through the existing validation path.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading should prevent crashes when package components omit their type. Metadata deduction should succeed for valid packages that mix typed and untyped components, while still rejecting explicitly incompatible component type declarations.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the accepted behavior for components explicitly marked as `PackageType.SHARED` or `PackageType.STATIC`. Do not relax validation for components with libraries and an explicitly unsupported type; only eliminate the erroneous failure caused by handling an unset type like a `PackageType` value.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing valid shared and static library behavior, keep invalid type declarations rejected, and remove only the unintended failure caused by an unspecified type.

behavior: `deduce_full_cpp_info()` no longer fails when a component with libraries has no explicit `type`.
Packages with multiple components can mix explicitly typed and untyped components without triggering a runtime error during `cpp_info` deduction.
Automatic library deduction continues to accept components explicitly declared as shared or static, and also accepts components with no declared type.
A component that declares libraries and explicitly uses an incompatible type still fails with `ConanException`.
acceptance_criteria: When a package defines multiple components and one component exposes libraries without an explicit type while another component declares a type, dependency metadata generation should complete without a runtime type-comparison failure.
When `deduce_full_cpp_info()` runs on a component with libraries and no explicit type, it should continue deduction instead of failing because an unset type is treated as a `PackageType`.
When a component with libraries explicitly declares `PackageType.SHARED` or `PackageType.STATIC`, deduction should remain valid.
When a component with libraries explicitly declares an incompatible type, the operation should fail with Conan's normal validation error.

task_27.title: Fix Python environment installs for pip version ranges and migrate to PyEnv
task_27.description: The update fixes Conan's Python virtual environment helper so pip requirement specifiers with version ranges install correctly, and introduces PyEnv as the preferred API while keeping PipEnv and its interpreter configuration as deprecated compatibility paths.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recipes using the Python virtual environment helper can install pip requirements that include version ranges without command-line parsing failures, while providing a supported upgrade path from PipEnv to PyEnv and preserving compatibility for existing PipEnv consumers through deprecation warnings.

expectation.grounded: Expose `conan.tools.system.PyEnv` as the preferred Python virtual environment manager. `PyEnv.install(packages, pip_args=None)` must pass each package specifier to pip as a single argument so requirement strings such as version ranges remain intact during installation. `PyEnv.generate()` must continue to expose the virtual environment on `PATH`, and `PyEnv.run(args)` must execute commands with the environment's Python interpreter. `PipEnv` must remain callable as a deprecated compatibility alias of `PyEnv`, and the deprecated `tools.system.pipenv:python_interpreter` configuration must still be accepted with a deprecation warning in favor of `tools.system.pyenv:python_interpreter`. If no Python interpreter can be resolved, virtual environment creation fails, or `py_version` is requested from Python versions below 3.8, a `ConanException` must be raised.
expectation.conceptual: The Python environment helper should accept normal pip dependency syntax, including ranged version constraints, without the shell misinterpreting those constraints. Users should be guided toward the new PyEnv name and configuration key, but existing PipEnv-based recipes should continue to work during the deprecation period. When a specific Python version is requested, the helper should either create that environment successfully or fail clearly when the runtime does not support it.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress standard virtual environment creation, package installation, or environment activation for existing Conan recipes. Continue resolving the interpreter from `tools.system.pyenv:python_interpreter` first, then the deprecated `tools.system.pipenv:python_interpreter`, then the system default Python executable. Keep `PipEnv` available as a compatibility entry point rather than removing it in this release.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break ordinary Python environment workflows. Backward compatibility should be preserved for existing recipes, with warnings instead of immediate removal, and interpreter selection should remain predictable when explicit configuration is present.

behavior: `PyEnv` is introduced as the preferred Conan helper for creating and using Python virtual environments.
`PipEnv` remains usable but now behaves as a deprecated compatibility alias that emits a deprecation warning.
The preferred interpreter configuration key is `tools.system.pyenv:python_interpreter`, while `tools.system.pipenv:python_interpreter` is still honored with a deprecation warning.
`PyEnv.install()` preserves pip requirement specifiers as single install arguments, so expressions with version ranges are installed correctly instead of being broken by shell parsing.
When `py_version` is provided, `PyEnv` creates a version-specific virtual environment and rejects that mode with `ConanException` on Python runtimes earlier than 3.8.
If Conan cannot resolve a Python interpreter or cannot create the requested virtual environment, the helper fails with `ConanException` rather than silently continuing.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan recipe installs a pip requirement using a version range such as `package>=x,<y` through the Python environment helper, the installation should succeed without the range expression being misinterpreted by the shell.
When a recipe uses `conan.tools.system.PyEnv`, it should be able to create a virtual environment, install packages into it, and expose that environment for subsequent Conan steps.
When a recipe still uses `PipEnv`, it should continue to work in this release but should emit a deprecation warning directing users to `PyEnv`.

When the deprecated `tools.system.pipenv:python_interpreter` configuration is used, Conan should still honor it but should emit a deprecation warning directing users to `tools.system.pyenv:python_interpreter`.
When no configured or default Python interpreter can be found, the helper should fail with `ConanException` instead of creating a partial environment.
When a specific Python version is requested on a runtime older than Python 3.8, the helper should fail with `ConanException` rather than attempting unsupported environment creation.

task_29.title: Fix CMakeConfigDeps transitive libraries in build context
task_29.description: Conan 2.25.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so transitive library dependencies remain available when packages are consumed in the build context. Direct build requirements still keep their special handling, but libraries reached through them now generate the expected CMake link targets.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps correctly exposes transitive library dependencies when generating build-context dependencies, so a build requirement that depends on libraries can still provide usable CMake library targets to downstream consumers.

expectation.grounded: CMakeConfigDeps should generate imported library targets for non-build transitive requirements even when the dependency graph is being generated in the build context. Direct build requirements should continue to avoid generating library targets, while existing executable target generation remains available.
expectation.conceptual: When a tool or other build-context package depends on a library, that transitive library should appear as a normal CMake dependency that downstream projects can resolve and link. The special treatment of direct build tools should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress host-context dependency generation. Do not start exposing direct build requirements themselves as library targets. Preserve the distinction between direct build requirements and their non-build transitive dependencies.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped: it should restore missing transitive library visibility in build context without changing how ordinary host dependencies work or turning every build-only package into a linkable library target.

behavior: Generated CMake dependency data now includes library targets for transitive dependencies reached from a build-context requirement when those transitive dependencies are regular libraries.
Library target generation is no longer blocked solely because the consuming dependency graph is in build context.
Direct build requirements continue to omit library target generation, preserving their existing build-tool semantics.
Executable target generation for dependencies is unaffected by this change.
acceptance_criteria: When CMakeConfigDeps generates files for a build requirement that depends on a library package, the transitive library should be exposed through an imported CMake library target.
When the dependency being generated is itself a direct build requirement, it should not become a generated library target merely because build-context files are produced.
When the same dependency graph is generated in host context, existing library target behavior should remain unchanged.
When downstream CMake code references a transitive library coming from a build-context dependency chain, it should be able to resolve that target without special-case handling.

task_28.title: Fix case-sensitive symlink pattern matching in files.copy
task_28.description: The 2.25.0 update fixes a bug in `conan.tools.files.copy()` so glob patterns are evaluated consistently for symlinked directories. Patterns that include uppercase path segments now match symlink entries correctly when case-sensitive matching is used, and case-insensitive matching is applied consistently when requested.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan.tools.files.copy()` correctly matches symlinked directory paths against the requested glob pattern, including paths with uppercase characters, so matching symlink entries are copied under the same case-sensitivity rules as other copy candidates.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.files.copy()` evaluates source entries, symlinked directories must be matched against the provided `pattern` using the same `ignore_case` behavior as regular file paths. With `ignore_case=False`, symlink paths must be compared using their original relative-path casing. With `ignore_case=True`, both the pattern and symlink relative paths must be normalized for case-insensitive matching before deciding whether the symlinked directory is included in the copy result.
expectation.conceptual: Copy operations should treat symlinked directories like other matched inputs: case-sensitive copies should respect exact path casing, and case-insensitive copies should match regardless of letter case. Users should not lose matching symlink entries just because the path or pattern contains uppercase characters.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public `conan.tools.files.copy()` API or its existing glob-based filtering model. Preserve current exclusion handling and the existing matching behavior for non-symlink file entries; the fix must only correct how symlinked directory paths are compared to `pattern` under `ignore_case`.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting symlink match behavior without altering how normal file copies, exclusions, or the overall copy interface work.

behavior: Symlinked directory entries are included in copy candidates only when their relative path matches the requested glob pattern under the configured case-sensitivity mode.
With `ignore_case=False`, symlinked directory matching uses the original relative path instead of a lowercased form, so patterns containing uppercase path segments can match correctly.
With `ignore_case=True`, case normalization is applied consistently before matching symlinked directories, aligning symlink behavior with regular file matching.
acceptance_criteria: When a source tree contains a symlink to a directory whose relative path includes uppercase characters, calling `conan.tools.files.copy()` with a matching glob pattern and `ignore_case=False` should copy that symlink entry.
When `conan.tools.files.copy()` is called with `ignore_case=True`, a symlinked directory should match the glob pattern regardless of case differences between the pattern and the symlink path.
When the symlinked directory path does not match the pattern under the active case-sensitivity mode, it should not be copied.
Regular non-symlink file matching behavior should remain unchanged by this fix.

task_30.title: Fix update to remote revisions already cached locally
task_30.description: Conan 2.25.0 fixes revision update handling so `--update` can move to the remote's latest recipe revision even when that exact revision already exists in the local cache with an older local timestamp. Instead of failing or leaving the wrong cached revision selected, Conan now reuses the cached revision and refreshes its cache ordering so the remote-selected revision becomes current.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that updating dependencies from a remote can switch to the remote's latest recipe revision even if that revision is already present in the local cache with an older timestamp, and ensure the cache reflects that revision as the current latest local revision instead of failing or keeping a different revision active.

expectation.grounded: When resolving a recipe reference with `--update`, if the remote revision differs from the current cached revision and the remote timestamp is newer, Conan must treat the remote revision as the authoritative latest revision. If retrieving that revision encounters `ConanReferenceAlreadyExistsInDB` because the same revision is already stored in the cache, Conan must reuse the cached recipe layout for that revision, update its local recipe timestamp so it becomes the latest cached revision, and report the reference as updated rather than failing.
expectation.conceptual: An update operation should follow the remote's newest revision, even when that revision was seen before and is already cached locally. If the remote moves back to a previously cached revision, the client should adopt that revision successfully and make it the active latest cached copy.

constraints.grounded: Do not fail or require a duplicate download when the target remote revision already exists in the local cache. Preserve normal update behavior when the remote revision is actually new, and preserve existing non-update behavior when no newer remote revision should be selected. Only refresh cache ordering for the revision that matches the remote-selected latest revision.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only change how updates reconcile remote and cached revision metadata. It must not introduce duplicate cached revisions, unnecessary downloads, or changes to cases where no update is needed.

behavior: If `--update` detects that a remote has a different recipe revision whose remote timestamp is newer than the currently selected cached revision, Conan should proceed with an update.
If that remote revision is not yet present in the local cache, Conan should keep the existing behavior of downloading it and marking the recipe as updated.

If that remote revision already exists in the local cache but is older in local timestamp ordering, Conan should reuse the cached revision, refresh its local recipe timestamp, and mark the recipe as updated.
A remote reverting to a previously published recipe revision should no longer cause the update flow to fail because the revision already exists in the cache.
acceptance_criteria: Given a recipe reference whose latest remote revision differs from the currently selected cached revision, when the user runs a command with `--update`, Conan should resolve to the remote's latest revision and report it as updated.

Given that the remote's latest revision already exists in the local cache with an older local timestamp, when the user runs a command with `--update`, Conan should succeed without an already-exists failure, reuse the cached revision, and make that revision the latest local cached revision afterward.
When a remote switches back to a previously known revision, an update operation should adopt that reverted revision successfully instead of leaving a different cached revision active.
When no newer remote revision should be selected, existing non-update behavior and normal cache contents should remain unchanged.

task_31.title: Correct exclusive graph-context package listing
task_31.description: Conan 2.25.0 fixes `conan list --graph` filtering for `--graph-context=build-only` and `--graph-context=host-only` so results no longer include unintended packages when the same dependency appears in both contexts with binary mismatches or skipped binaries. Exclusive-context output now removes non-exclusive package entries and omits recipes that have no remaining packages in the selected context.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan list --graph=... --graph-context=build-only|host-only` returns only packages that are exclusive to the requested graph context, and does not surface unintended recipes or binaries when the same dependency appears in both host and build contexts with package binary mismatches or skipped binaries.

expectation.grounded: When `conan list` loads a graph file with `--graph-context=build-only` or `--graph-context=host-only`, it should scope nodes to the requested base context and exclude any package entry whose `PkgReference` also exists in the opposite context of the same graph. If removing those package entries leaves a recipe with no remaining packages in the selected `PackagesList`, that recipe should no longer be listed. This filtering should apply even when the opposite-context occurrence differs in binary state or related metadata.
expectation.conceptual: Exclusive graph-context listing should behave as a true context-only view. If a package is represented in both host and build contexts, it should not appear in `build-only` or `host-only` results just because the binaries differ or one side was skipped; only packages unique to the selected context should remain, and recipes with no remaining packages should disappear.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to `conan list --graph` handling of `--graph-context=build-only` and `--graph-context=host-only`. Other listing modes, including unfiltered graph listings and base `build` or `host` context selection, should preserve existing behavior. Packages that are present only in the requested context must continue to be listed together with their recipe entries.
constraints.conceptual: Only the exclusive-context filtering semantics should change. Standard graph listings must stay stable, and genuinely context-specific packages must still be visible.

behavior: `conan list --graph=... --graph-context=build-only` and `--graph-context=host-only` now behave as exclusive context views rather than simple raw node-context filters.
Package entries that share the same recipe reference and package ID across host and build contexts are removed from exclusive-context results.
This exclusion works even when the host and build occurrences differ in binary status or metadata, preventing unintended package leakage caused by binary mismatches.
If all package entries for a recipe are removed by exclusive-context filtering, that recipe is omitted from the output instead of remaining as an empty match.
Recipes and package binaries that exist only in the selected context remain listed.
acceptance_criteria: When a graph contains the same dependency package in both host and build contexts, running `conan list --graph=... --graph-context=build-only` should not show that shared package in the output.
When a graph contains the same dependency package in both host and build contexts, running `conan list --graph=... --graph-context=host-only` should not show that shared package in the output.

When the same recipe appears in both contexts but the package binary differs between them, each exclusive-context listing should show only the package binary belonging to its own context and should not include the opposite-context binary.
When exclusive-context filtering removes every package under a recipe, the recipe should no longer appear in the listing.
When a package exists only in the requested context, exclusive-context listing should continue to include that recipe and package.
